Rashi on Ketubot 23a:10:1.hebrew: דרב המנונא - דאמר האשה שאמרה לבעלה "גירשתני" נאמנת, הלכך הא דאמרה "גרושה אני" מהימנא:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:10:1.english: [In accordance with] Rav Hamnuna - Who said [that] a woman who says to her husband, "You divorced me," is believed; therefore, this [woman] who says, "I am divorced," is believed.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:13:1.english: And I have witnesses - Who were with me constantly, [such] that I was not secluded with an idolater.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:13:2.hebrew: ואח"כ באו עדים - שנשבית, דהשתא לאו הפה שאסר הוא, אפי' הכי לא תצא:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:13:2.english: And thereafter witnesses came - [testifying] that she was taken captive, so that now it is not [a case of] "the mouth that forbade [is the mouth that permitted]" — even so, she does not leave [her husband].

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:13:3.hebrew: אפי' יש לה כמה בנים - מן הכהן הזה שנשאה:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:13:3.english: Even if she has several children - From this priest who married her.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:14:1.english: Who came to Neharde'a - To be redeemed.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:15:1.hebrew: אוקמינהו לשבויינהו אבראי - שלא יבואו לפני ב"ד, ולא ידעו ב"ד שהן שבויות אלא ע"פ עצמן, ויתירום:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:15:1.english: They stationed their captors outside - So that [the captors] would not come before the court, and the court would not know that they were captives except by their own [word], and [thus the court] would permit them.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:16:1.hebrew: בנן דמוריין אינון - בנות אדם גדול ובעל הוראה הוא, שידעו לעשות הן:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:16:1.english: They are daughters of authorities - [These are] the daughters of a great man and a halakhic authority, for they knew [what] to do.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:17:1.english: To Rav Shemen - He was a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:17:2.english: Tend to your relatives - Marry one of them, for they are your relatives.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:17:3.hebrew: והא איכא סהדי במדינת הים - שראו שנשבו, ודלמא אתו לקמן למחר וליומא אוחרן לאחר שתנשא:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:17:3.english: But aren't there witnesses in a country overseas - who saw that they were taken captive, and perhaps they will come before us tomorrow or another day, after she marries?

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:17:4.hebrew: השתא מיהא לא איתנהו - קודם נישואין, ומשום דלמא אתו, לא אסרינן לה השתא:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:17:4.english: Now, in any event, they are not [here] - before marriage; and because perhaps they will come, we do not forbid her now.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:17:5.english: Witnesses in the astan side - In the north side. ["From the north gold comes" (Job 37:22) is translated in the Targum as mid'istana.]

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:17:6.hebrew: ותאסר - בתמיה. הא אתו — קודם נשואין:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:17:6.english: And will she be forbidden - [This is] a rhetorical question. [And the Gemara's inference,] "if they came" — [this means] before marriage.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:2:1.hebrew: תרוייהו בפנויה קמסהדי - לדברי שניהם, עד עכשיו בחזקת פנויה היתה [קודם שנתקדשה]:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:2:1.english: Both of them testify [that she was] unmarried - According to both of them, until now she had the presumptive status of an unmarried woman [before she was betrothed].

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:4:1.hebrew: איפוך - ברישא תני אם ניסת תצא, וסיפא אם ניסת לא תצא:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:4:1.english: Reverse - In the first clause, teach "if she married, she must leave," and [in] the latter clause, "if she married, she need not leave."

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:7:1.english: That they divorce in private - And even so, she should not marry in the first instance, because of slanderous talk.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:8:1.hebrew: ארישא - אם משניסת באו עדים שהיתה אשת איש, והיא ניסת על פי עצמה שאמרה גרושה אני:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:8:1.english: To the first clause - If after she married, witnesses came [testifying] that she was a married woman, while she had married on her own word, for she had said, "I am a divorcée."

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:8:2.hebrew: אסיפא - אנשביתי וטהורה אני, והתירוה לינשא, ואח"כ באו עדים שנשבית:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:8:2.english: To the latter clause - [Referring] to [the case where she says,] "I was taken captive and I am pure," and they permitted her to marry, and afterward witnesses came [testifying] that she was taken captive.

Rashi on Ketubot 23a:9:1.hebrew: בשבויה הקילו - דחששא בעלמא הוא דאיכא, שמא נבעלה לעובד כוכבים ונפסלה לכהונה:
Rashi on Ketubot 23a:9:1.english: With a captive woman they were lenient - For it is merely a concern that exists, lest she had intercourse with an idolater and became disqualified from [marrying into] the priesthood.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:10:1.hebrew: אית ליה דרב המנונא - אע"ג דרב המנונא איירי בפניו, מ"מ לענין ניסת ואח"כ באו עדים מהני שלא בפניו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:10:1.english: He holds [in accordance with the presumption] of Rav Hamnuna - Even though Rav Hamnuna is speaking [specifically of a claim made] in his [husband's] presence, nevertheless, with regard to [a case where] she married and afterward witnesses came, [it] is effective [even] not in his presence.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:12:1.hebrew: לא תצא מהיתרה הראשון - פירוש: ותנשא [לכתחלה], דלא שייך לזות שפתים כלל. אבל אין לפרש כי ההיא דיבמות, דלא תצא מהיתרה הראשון לענין דאם נשאת לא תצא, אבל לכתחלה לא תינשא — כדמשמע גבי בנתיה דמר שמואל בסמוך, שהתירן לכתחילה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:12:1.english: She does not emerge from her initial permitted [status] - Explanation: [this means] that she may marry [ab initio], for "crookedness of the lips" [i.e., suspicion] does not apply at all. However, one should not explain [it] like that [case] in Yevamot, where "she does not emerge from her initial permitted [status]" [is only] with respect to [the rule] that if she [already] married, she does not leave [her husband], but ab initio she may not marry — as is implied regarding the daughters of Mar Shmuel shortly below, whom he permitted [to marry] ab initio.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:13:1.hebrew: באו עדים לא תצא - פירוש: לא תצא מהיתרה הראשון:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:13:1.english: "Witnesses came... she need not leave" - Explanation: she does not leave [i.e., lose] her initial permission [to marry].

Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:14:1.hebrew: עד האידנא מאן נטרינהו - פי' דכבר נאסרו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:14:1.english: Until now who guarded them - [The] explanation [is] that they have already become forbidden [to the priesthood].

Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:17:1.hebrew: והא איכא עדים במדינת הים - אין לפרש "דלמא איכא עדים במדינת הים", דאם כן תיקשי ליה נמי אמתניתין דקתני "נשביתי וטהורה אני — נאמנת", ואמאי? דלמא איכא עדים! אלא הכי פירושה: הא יצא קול דאיכא עדים במדינת הים שיודעים שנשבית. ומיהו קשה לרשב"א: דהיכי סלקא דעתיה השתא דעדים היינו עדי שבויה? דא"כ, מה הוה צריך למימר "הא איכא עדים במדינת הים"? הוה ליה למימר "הא איכא עדים קמן", דהא איכא שבויינהו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:17:1.english: But aren't there witnesses in a country overseas - One cannot explain [this as meaning], "Perhaps there are witnesses in a country overseas," for if so, he should also have raised a difficulty against the Mishnah, which teaches: "[If a woman says,] 'I was taken captive, yet I am pure,' she is believed" — and why [should she be believed]? Perhaps there are witnesses [overseas]! Rather, this is its explanation: "Behold, a rumor has gone out that there are witnesses in a country overseas who know that she was taken captive." However, [this] is difficult for the Rashba: how could [the Gemara] think at this point that "witnesses" means witnesses of captivity? For if so, why did he need to say, "Behold, there are witnesses in a country overseas"? He should have said, "Behold, there are witnesses before us," for their captors are here.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:18:1.hebrew: עדי טומאה איתמר - "והא איכא עדים במדינת הים" דפריך לעיל, פירוש: והא יצא קול דאיכא התם עדי טומאה, כדפירשתי. הקשה ר"ת בפרק קמא דקידושין (דף יב.) גבי ההוא גברא דקדיש באבנא דכוחלא, ויתיב רב חסדא וקא משער אי אית בה שוה פרוטה אי לא, ומסיק: לאו היינו דר' חנינא דאמר "עדים בצד אסתן ותאסר", וקאמר: אביי ורבא לא סבירא להו הא דרב חסדא — אם הקילו בשבויה, נקל באשת איש? והשתא למאי דמסיק דעדי טומאה איתמר, מה לי עדי שבויה, מה לי עדי אשת איש? ורש"י פירש שם: "אם הקילו בשבויה" — דאיסור לאו. וקשה לרבינו תם, דבשבויה נמי איכא איסור סקילה אם נשאת לכהן, שישמש בנה על גבי מזבח בשבת. ומיהו אית ספרים דגרסי התם: "אם הקילו בשבויה" — דמנוולה נפשה באפי שבויה כו'; פירוש: ולא שכיח כולי האי שנטמאה, נקל באשת איש דשכיח דידעי אם אית בה שוה פרוטה? ובלאו הך גירסא איכא למימר דלא שכיח שיהו עדי טומאה, אבל עדים שידעו ששוה פרוטה שכיח:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:18:1.english: [The discussion] was stated [with regard to] witnesses of violation - [Regarding] "But there are witnesses in a distant land" that [the Gemara] asks above, the explanation is: "But a rumor has gone out that there are witnesses of violation there," as I explained [earlier]. Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty in the first chapter of Kiddushin (12a) regarding a certain man who betrothed [a woman] with a stone of kohl, and Rav Chisda sat and was estimating whether it had the value of a perutah or not, and [the Gemara] concludes: Is this not [the same as] that [statement] of Rabbi Chanina, who said, "There are witnesses in the north, and should she be forbidden?!" And [the Gemara] says: Abaye and Rava do not hold of this [reasoning] of Rav Chisda — if they were lenient with a captive woman, shall we be lenient with a married woman? And now, according to what [our Gemara] concludes, that [Rav Ashi's statement] was said regarding witnesses of violation, what is the difference between witnesses of a captive woman and witnesses of a married woman? Rashi explained there: "If they were lenient with a captive woman" — for [her prohibition to a priest is only] a negative commandment. And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam, because with a captive woman there is also a prohibition punishable by stoning if she marries a priest, for her son will serve on the altar on Shabbat. However, there are texts that read there: "If they were lenient with a captive woman" — because she makes herself repulsive before her captors, etc.; explanation: and it is not so common that she was violated — shall we be lenient with a married woman, where it is common that [people] know whether it is worth a perutah? And even without this reading, one can say that it is not common for there to be witnesses of violation, whereas witnesses who know that it is worth a perutah is common:

Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:1:1.hebrew: מאי שנא רישא ומאי שנא סיפא - ואם תאמר: שנא ושנא! דרישא אית לן לאוקמה בחזקת פנויה, וסיפא בחזקת אשת איש. ויש לומר: דברישא, אע"ג דאית לן לאוקמה בחזקת פנויה, מ"מ תרי ותרי ספיקא דרבנן היא, כדמוכח בפרק ד' אחין (יבמות דף לא. ושם), והוה לן למימר תצא מדרבנן. וי"מ: כיון דלא מפליג בין באו עדים עד שלא ניסת לבאו עדים משניסת, ש"מ דלאו רבי מנחם בר יוסי היא אלא רבנן; א"כ, סיפא נמי אמאי תצא? הא שמעינן להו דאמרי לא תצא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:1:1.english: What is different [in] the first clause, and what is different [in] the second clause - And if you should ask: Indeed they are different! For [in] the first clause we must establish her in her presumptive status of an unmarried woman, whereas [in] the second clause [we must establish her] in her presumptive status of a married woman. And one can answer: In the first clause, even though we must establish her in her presumptive status of an unmarried woman, nevertheless, two [witnesses] against two [witnesses] is a rabbinic doubt, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin (Yevamot 31a and elsewhere), and we would have said [that] she must leave [her husband] by rabbinic law. And some explain: Since [the baraita] does not distinguish between [a case where] witnesses came before she married and [a case where] witnesses came after she married, learn from this that it is not [the opinion of] Rabbi Menachem bar Yose, but rather [that of] the Rabbis; if so, in the second clause as well, why must she leave? Surely we have heard them say [that] she need not leave.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:2:1.hebrew: תרוייהו בפנויה קמסהדי - לא הוה צריך להא, דאפי' ליכא אלא ההוא דאמר "נתקדשה" לא תצא, דאין דבר שבערוה פחות משנים. אבל תימה: אמאי לא תנשא לכתחלה, דהוה לן לאוקמה אחזקה? וי"ל: כגון שאנו יודעים שזרק לה קדושין, ומספקא לן אי קרוב לו או קרוב לה, והני ב' סהדי — חד אמר "קרוב לו" וחד אמר "קרוב לה" — דכיון דודאי זרק לה הקדושין, לית לן למימר "אוקמה אחזקה" להתירה לכתחילה. אי נמי: כגון שהיו נרות דולקות ומטות מוצעות שהיה עומד לקדש, כדאמר בסוף המגרש (גיטין פט.), ועד אחד אומר "נתקדשה" ועד אחד אומר "לא נתקדשה" באותה שעה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:2:1.english: They are both testifying that she was unmarried - [The Gemara] did not need this [reasoning], for even if there were only the one who says "she was betrothed," she would not have to leave [her husband], because a matter of marital status is not [established] with fewer than two [witnesses]. However, it is puzzling: why may she not marry ab initio, since we should establish her on her presumptive status [of being unmarried]? And one can answer: [this refers to a case] such as where we know that he threw betrothal [money] to her, and we are in doubt whether [it landed] closer to him or closer to her, and these two witnesses — one says "closer to him" and one says "closer to her" — for since he certainly threw the betrothal [money] to her, we do not say "establish her on her presumptive status" to permit her [to marry] ab initio. Alternatively, [it refers to a case] such as where candles were lit and beds were spread, [indicating] that he was about to betroth [her], as [the Gemara] says at the end of [the chapter] HaMegaresh (Gittin 89a), and one witness says "she was betrothed" and one witness says "she was not betrothed" at that time.

Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:9:1.hebrew: מאן דמתני לה ארישא כל שכן אסיפא - וא"ת: מנא ליה? דלמא אסיפא לא מצי קאי, דאפי' באו עדים ואחר כך נשאת — לא תצא. ולמאי דמפרש בסמוך, לא ניסת ניסת ממש — אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 23a:9:1.english: The one who taught it [in reference] to the first clause, all the more so [in reference] to the latter clause - And if you ask: From where does he [know] this? Perhaps [this ruling] cannot apply to the latter clause, for [there,] even if witnesses came and afterward she married, she does not leave [her husband]. And according to what [the Gemara] explains shortly — [that] "she married" does not [mean] she actually married [but rather that the court permitted her to marry] — it works out well.
